settings:36511.title: FailSafe
settings:36511.summary: A safety watchdog. The AX keeps checking its CTs (the clamps that measure current) and its other inputs. If anything looks wrong, it tells the inverters to drop to low generation.
settings:36511.write_explain: Write the code directly, using the extension's numbering: 0 Off, 1 Normal, 2 Shutdown, 3 No Communication, 4 Force Limit. Tauri's labels for the same codes are believed wrong and are kept only in the conflict record.
settings:36511.gotcha: This is protection, not an on/off switch. The AX keeps checking its CTs (the clamps that measure current) and its other inputs; if anything is wrong it tells the inverters to go to low generation. A fault must never let a site keep exporting freely. Tauri labels these same codes as ramp modes (Hard Limit / Ramp Down / Ramp Up / Ramp Both) — that reading is not trusted.
sources: Tanner, 2026-08-21 — FailSafe checks CTs and other inputs; on a fault it commands inverters to low generation
settings:36511.overrides_do_not_write: Tanner, 2026-08-21 — the extension's codes are trusted. Its EpmAx tables were the ones that proved right about codes on PV, and its config layer is the only source carrying a real note per setting.

settings:36551.title: Control Protocol
settings:36551.summary: Picks which language the AX uses to talk to the inverters: Modbus, or the older 7E protocol.
settings:36551.write_explain: Write the code directly, using the extension's numbering: 0 is 7E Protocol, 1 is Modbus. Tauri has these reversed.
settings:36551.gotcha: Both apps agree this selects Modbus vs the older 7E protocol; they disagreed on the codes and the extension's order is the one used here. 7E works on all grid-tied inverters but may cause problems with hybrid inverters — so on a mixed site, Modbus is usually the safer choice.
sources: SolisDebuggerToolExtension/src/config/EpmAx/controlSettings.ts — '7E protocol works on all grid-tied inverters but may cause issues with hybrid inverters'
settings:36551.overrides_do_not_write: Tanner, 2026-08-21 — the extension's codes are trusted, same reasoning as failSafe.

settings:36549.title: Meter 1 select
settings:36549.summary: One register holding two separate settings — the meter's make in the low byte, and where it is fitted in the high byte.
settings:36549.write_explain: Read the register, change only the byte you mean to change, then write the whole word back. Writing a bare number clears the other byte.
settings:36549.gotcha: Low byte is the meter type (0 Acrel, 1 Eastron, 2 Rayleigh, 3 Rayleigh F, 4 No Meter). High byte is where it sits (0 Grid, 1 Load, 2 Other PV, 3 Total PV, 4 Generator, 5 N/A). Writing '1' meaning 'Eastron' also sets the location to Grid, because the high byte becomes zero.

settings:36509.title: Inverter quantity
settings:36509.summary: One register holding two counts — how many PV inverters in the low byte, how many hybrid inverters in the high byte.
settings:36509.write_explain: Read, change one byte, write the whole word back. These are counts, not codes.
settings:36509.gotcha: On the EPM this same address is a single plain count called 'Inverter number'. On the AX it is two counts in one word. Writing an EPM-style count here sets the PV quantity and zeroes the hybrid quantity.
